data.title: Vizsla Silver Revises Panuco First Silver Production Target to H2 2028
data.description:
Vizsla Silver ( (TSE:VZLA) ) has provided an update.

On Nov. 19, 2026, Vizsla Silver reported continued development of its wholly owned Panuco silver-gold project in Mexico, with work focused on construction readiness. M3 Engineering & Technology had completed approximately 50% of engineering, and approximately 85% of contemplated process-plant equipment had been ordered.

Three development contracts had been awarded for engineering procurement and construction management, mine design and equipment supply, while the main mining contract remained to be awarded. The company also said it was working with Mexican federal authorities and third-party security advisers on preparations for a phased return to site.

Vizsla revised its targeted first silver-production date to the second half of 2028 from the second half of 2027, citing expectations for permitting, site readiness and construction timing. It committed an initial US$5 million to a planned Vizsla Foundation intended to support education, health and economic development in communities surrounding Panuco.

The company did not update the operating, capital or economic parameters from its November 2025 feasibility study and said it had made no production decision. The revised timeline marked a one-year delay to the targeted production start while development planning and security preparations continued.

data.title: Beeline Holdings Enters Agreement for TYTL Merger
data.description:
Beeline Holdings ( (BLNE) ) has issued an announcement.

On November 19, 2026, Beeline Holdings entered an agreement under which its wholly owned subsidiary would merge into TYTL, leaving TYTL as Beeline’s wholly owned subsidiary. On November 18, Beeline’s independent special committee unanimously approved the transaction and recommended stockholder approval after retaining independent counsel; it also required a fairness opinion and majority-of-the-minority voting protections.

The agreement provided for TYTL stockholders to receive shares representing approximately 40% of Beeline’s post-closing equity on a fully diluted basis, while pre-merger Beeline holders would represent approximately 60%. After the cancellation of one-third of Chief Executive Officer Nicholas Liuzza’s merger shares, TYTL holders would receive approximately 37% assuming no additional Beeline issuance.

Liuzza’s merger shares were subject to a 24-month lock-up and staged release conditions tied to $100 million and $200 million market capitalizations, while other TYTL stockholders’ shares were subject to 12-month lock-ups. Closing was conditioned on stockholder approvals and TYTL obtaining at least $15 million in specified non-debt financing; TYTL’s audited financial statements for January 3 through December 31, 2025, reported negative operating cash flows, reliance on related-party advances and equity financing, and substantial doubt about its ability to continue as a going concern.

data.title: IceCure Medical Earnings Call Highlights Growth and Risks
data.description:
Icecure Medical Ltd. ((ICCM)) has held its Q3 earnings call. Read on for the main highlights of the call.

The call was generally positive, with revenue growth, stronger U.S. sales and wider adoption of ProSense outweighing the company’s larger losses and lower cash balance. Management highlighted clinical and international progress, although uncertainty remains around the timing of ChoICE enrollment and the early stage of the commercial opportunity.

Revenue and U.S. Sales Growth

IceCure reported first-nine-month 2026 revenue of about $2.6 million, up 26% from $2.1 million a year earlier. U.S. sales rose 83%, supported by expanded commercial activity and growing adoption of ProSense.

Gross Profit Improvement

Gross profit increased about 22% to $762,000 from $626,000 in the comparable 2025 period. The improvement reflected the company’s higher revenue base, although profitability remains well below the level needed to cover operating costs.

Expanded U.S. Commercial Footprint

By the end of the third quarter, IceCure had expanded its U.S. commercial presence from 11 states to 21 states. It also added sales, marketing and clinical support staff in New York, Southern California, the Midwest and Florida to encourage ProSense use.

Expected Continued Revenue Momentum

Management said U.S. sales should continue rising from quarter to quarter and noted that the fourth quarter is usually the company’s strongest. It also described the 2027 revenue outlook as healthy double-digit growth, while stressing that formal guidance was not being provided.

ChoICE Study Clinical Progress

IceCure said the ChoICE post-marketing study had established sites at West Cancer Center in Tennessee, Adventist Health Glendale in California and Legacy Health in Portland, Oregon. During the question-and-answer session, management said four sites were active and patients had begun enrolling and receiving treatment.

Positive Early Feedback From New Users

Management reported favorable early feedback from Dr. Nathalie Johnson, identified as a new ProSense user at the Portland site. She reportedly found the system easy to use and viewed it as an excellent, minimally invasive solution after being highly satisfied with the cases performed.

Additional ChoICE Sites and Patient Pipeline

The company said it was recruiting and contracting with additional clinical sites, including locations that already had suitable patients waiting for treatment. Management expects a steadier pace of new site enrollment over the next several months.

International Regulatory and Distribution Expansion

ProSense received regulatory approval in China, while IceCure signed an exclusive distribution agreement in the Netherlands. Management also cited continued interest from physicians and institutions in Europe, South America and other international markets.

Additional Clinical Evidence

During the quarter, the company highlighted two peer-reviewed publications on cryoablation and treatment de-escalation in breast cancer. The research included work involving early-stage breast cancer and axillary lymph node metastasis, adding to the evidence supporting the technology.

Investment in Commercial and Clinical Capabilities

IceCure continues to invest in its U.S. commercial organization and in the ChoICE study. Management said these efforts are intended to build the commercial, clinical and organizational capabilities needed for broader ProSense adoption.

Intellectual Property Portfolio Development

The company said it is continuing to strengthen its intellectual property portfolio as ProSense enters more markets and gains commercial exposure. Management described the portfolio as an important strategic asset for the company’s long-term development.

International Expansion Pipeline

In China, IceCure is discussing potential distribution partners, while in Canada it has answered Health Canada’s questions and is awaiting a decision. Terumo is expected to submit ProSense to Japan’s PMDA during the first half of 2027, extending the company’s regulatory pipeline.

Operating and Net Loss Increased

IceCure’s first-nine-month 2026 operating and net loss was about $12.9 million, compared with $10.8 million in the prior-year period. The wider loss shows that the company is spending heavily to support clinical development and commercial expansion.

Higher Research and Development Expenses

Research and development costs rose to about $6.5 million from $5.1 million. The increase was mainly tied to the ChoICE post-marketing study and other clinical and product-development activities.

Higher Sales and Marketing Expenses

Sales and marketing expenses climbed about 20% to $3.6 million from $3.0 million. The increase primarily reflected the continued expansion of IceCure’s U.S. commercial operations and support team.

Cash Balance Declined

Cash and cash equivalents totaled about $8.2 million at Sept. 30, 2026, down from roughly $8.9 million at the end of 2025. The decline highlights the funding pressure associated with the company’s ongoing clinical and commercial investments.

ChoICE Enrollment Timeline Uncertainty

Management said it was not certain that ChoICE would enroll 400 patients within three years. Delays in site contracts, agreements and travel earlier in the year have made the final timing difficult to predict.

Seasonally Weaker Third-Quarter Revenue

Management characterized the third quarter as seasonally weaker, similar to the first quarter. The fourth quarter is typically the company’s best period, providing an important seasonal lift to annual revenue.

Commercial Opportunity Remains at an Early Stage

IceCure acknowledged that it is still in the early stages of realizing ProSense’s commercial potential. The expanding state footprint, larger support team and growing physician interest point to progress, but broad adoption remains a work in progress.

Forward-Looking Guidance

Management expects U.S. sales to keep increasing quarter over quarter and projects fourth-quarter 2026 revenue to exceed third-quarter revenue. It described next year’s revenue opportunity as healthy double-digit growth and plans to expand the team to support important double-digit U.S. growth, while noting that it is not issuing formal guidance.

The company also expects additional ChoICE sites to come online in the near term, although completing enrollment of 400 patients within three years remains uncertain. Health Canada approval could arrive within weeks or two to four months, and Terumo is expected to file in Japan during the first half of 2027.

IceCure’s earnings call presented a company gaining commercial reach and clinical momentum, particularly in the United States. However, rising losses, declining cash and uncertainty around study timing remain important risks as management invests in turning ProSense into a broader medical and commercial platform.

data.title: Burcon NutraScience Earnings Call Signals Growth Despite Setbacks
data.description:
Burcon Nutrascience Corporation ((TSE:BU)) has held its Q2 earnings call. Read on for the main highlights of the call.

Burcon NutraScience’s earnings call carried a strongly optimistic tone, led by nearly threefold year-over-year revenue growth, more than 40 buying customers and 209 active projects. Management also pointed to improving production, insider financing support and a path to positive cash flow, although an 18% sequential revenue decline, infrastructure constraints, an operating loss and a difficult external financing process remain concerns.

Revenue Growth Accelerates Year Over Year

Burcon reported that fiscal Q2 2027 revenue nearly tripled from the comparable quarter a year earlier. The increase was driven mainly by rising sales of the company’s plant-protein offerings, highlighting stronger commercial traction.

Customer Base and Sales Funnel Expand

The company surpassed 40 buying customers and reported 209 active projects. Management described this project base as the lifeblood of future growth, providing a broad pipeline beyond current sales.

Near-Term Pipeline Takes Shape

Of the 209 active projects, 26 have moved beyond the pallet-order stage. Management said these projects should support near-term growth in early to mid-2027 as customers advance toward broader launches.

GLP-1 Users Add to Specialty Protein Demand

Management said consumers taking GLP-1 weight-loss medications are seeking twice the protein with half the calories, supporting demand for specialty proteins. It estimated household penetration of these medications at roughly 20%, give or take.

Technology Supports Product Differentiation

Burcon said two decades of technology development have produced exceptionally pure proteins, supporting better taste, flavor and functionality for food manufacturers. The company is producing and selling pea, canola, fava and sunflower proteins.

Protein Applications Move Beyond Sports Nutrition

Protein-enhanced products are expanding into cereals, oatmeal, pasta, beverages and appetizers. Burcon is targeting everyday consumers who want higher protein without sacrificing taste or convenience.

Growth Expected From Three Customer Channels

Management said about one-third of growth should come from existing customers and products. Another third is expected from existing customers adding products, flavors or SKUs, with the remainder coming from new customers and projects.

Production Performance Improves

Burcon reported week-over-week improvement in daily production, efficiency and overall performance from late September through the earnings call. Management said infrastructure issues had been addressed, allowing production to move ahead of customer demand again.

Plant Schedule Set for Expansion

The plant currently operates five days per week around the clock. Burcon plans to shift to a seven-day, 24-hour schedule in the coming months to increase output and support customer requirements.

Operating Loss Improves Sequentially

The fiscal Q2 loss from operations declined 2% from the prior fiscal quarter, despite lower sequential sales. Lower cost of sales and reduced general and administrative expenses helped drive the improvement.

Scaling Could Improve Operating Leverage

Management said higher production and commercialization are improving efficiency and lowering operating costs relative to sales. It expects most fixed costs needed to scale the business to be in place by late this year or early 2027, allowing more contribution margin to reach profit.

Insider Financing Adds Working Capital

An entity related to board member James Pekar provided an unsecured loan of up to $4.2 million, maturing in November 2027. Burcon said the proceeds add working capital for operations, commercial production and plant-protein sales.

Investment Targets Capacity and Reliability

Burcon has invested in infrastructure reliability, protein capacity and staffing. Its operating partner, ProMan, supplies capital for the facility, while Burcon’s financing is focused mainly on people, reliability, working capital and inventory.

Licensing Could Shape the Longer-Term Model

Once the facility is operating near capacity and Burcon is financially stronger, management said the company may move toward a licensing model. Under that structure, operating margin could begin to converge with gross margin.

Sequential Revenue Fell on Shipment Timing

Fiscal Q2 2027 revenue declined 18% from Q1. Management attributed the decrease to shipment timing late in Q1, the production ramp and the additional infrastructure required to support manufacturing.

Infrastructure Issues Constrained Shipments

The manufacturing facility faced second-quarter challenges involving steam, water supplies and other plant support systems. Management characterized the problems as one-time issues that constrained shipments during the period.

New Customer Onboarding Temporarily Slowed

Burcon kept existing customers supplied during the production difficulties. However, it temporarily slowed new-customer onboarding to avoid sending an initial order that the company could not reliably deliver.

Company Remains Unprofitable

Burcon remains in an operating loss position despite the sequential improvement. The company said the 2% reduction in its operating loss reflects progress, but profitability has not yet been reached.

External Financing Process Continues

Management said it is pursuing a broader financing raise to strengthen the balance sheet and reach cash flow and profitability. It also acknowledged that market conditions are difficult for fundraising and said more information is expected in the coming weeks.

Staffing and Capacity Remain Constraints

The plant’s current five-day schedule limits available production time. Burcon also needs to remove manufacturing choke points and hire and train additional employees before it can fully expand capacity.

Management Points to a 2027 Breakout

Management expects significant sequential revenue growth in Q3 and sees a path to a more than $10 million revenue run rate, meaningful operating leverage and positive cash flow during calendar 2027. It described 2027 as a potential breakout year, while planning to move the plant to continuous seven-day operations in the coming months.

Overall, Burcon’s call showed a company moving from product development toward broader commercialization, with strong customer activity and improving production supporting the outlook. The main risks are near-term execution, financing, capacity and continued operating losses, but management’s growth and cash-flow targets gave the call a decidedly positive tone.
